fault: A caller from another Organization, or an assigned-scope caller without a grant, can use a Property they cannot reach (mayUsePermissionsOnProperties / isPropertyAccessibleForPermission).
An Organization-wide scope on one permission widens another permission's record visibility, or a permission missing from the scope map is not treated as 'none' (canForContext / scopeForPermission).
A server function is allowed without the Organization match, capability, role permission, active Property grant or consent it requires: decision order broken, or a deny turned into an allow.
Delayed worker, consumer or schedule work runs for a suspended or other Organization, with a missing scope or an unknown action, instead of failing closed.
A user with membership in two Organizations, or whose only membership is not the session's active Organization, is admitted.
A removed or role-downgraded member keeps access because a cached auth context is served past a permission_version change or an unreadable version.
A PropertyManager or Member role holds a permission reserved for the account owner (for example ai.manage or member.create).
A web request process can enter system database scope and read every Organization's rows, or a request's tenant scope leaks to another unit of work.
A pooled client runs a statement under the previous request's or job's tenant, or runs it after the scope setting failed.
A repository query omits the organization_id filter or returns soft-deleted rows, so another Organization's records are readable.
A lapsed or replaced Property access grant is kept as if it still gave access, or an active grant is superseded wrongly (decidePropertyGrant).
An assigned-scope manager acts on a Property without a current, unexpired grant, or a deny requirement collapses to an Organization-wide allow.
A second attempt publishes twice: an ambiguous or in-flight publication is authorized or claimed again, the idempotency key or cycle fails to advance, or a failure is misclassified as retryable.
Two workers claim the same authorized publication cycle, or a claim goes through with a duplicate provider operation key or a stale observation head (markPublicationSending).
An unreadable dispatch-evidence lookup counts as proof the attempt never left RepKey, so an ambiguous attempt is settled and sent again.
A Reply is claimed for publication on an archived Property, or one restored since approval (stale source epoch).
A provider call starts on a permit that is already started or fenced, or past its start deadline, or completes after its operation deadline.
One AI admission reaches the provider twice, or a forged or copied admission is accepted (mint and consume once).
An AI call is admitted for an operation that is not the executing attempt, or has another permit, source digest or authorization fence.
An AI result is admitted or written against a review source whose epoch, revision or digest changed, or whose content has expired (sourceHoldsOperation).
A stale or second worker claims or acts on a Google import item: wrong claim fence, dispatch epoch or retry revision, or an unexpired claim lease is overtaken.
An import item attempt beyond the attempt budget, or one that skips an ordinal, is admitted (importItemAdmitsAttempt off-by-one).
A Google sync or review write proceeds against a Property whose source epoch moved (archive, restore or relink), or takes locks out of the canonical order.
A worker with an expired or wrong lease token completes or fails work another worker now holds, or work runs past its max attempts.
An outbox consumer applies the same event twice on redelivery because its receipt is not honoured, or a failed consumer is silently dropped instead of failing the job.
A month, week or quarter boundary in the Property's timezone shifts a day, or a repeated DST hour resolves to the wrong local midnight (calendarPeriodRange / dayKeyInTimezone).
A DST gap or fold moves a Property-local day boundary by an hour or a day when shifting local days or converting wall-clock to an instant.
A Property-local calendar date or day count is off by one around midnight or DST.
A new goal starts in the wrong Property-local month: the day-20 cut-off, the current or next month option, or a stale month key after midnight is mishandled.
A due goal month is skipped, duplicated or opened before it begins, or catch-up runs past the version window (dueMonthlyPeriods / openResultsForPeriods).
A goal month closes before the reconciliation delay has passed or before source data reaches the month end (isGoalResultReadyToClose), or a monthly period is cut wrongly.
A Property-local Monday-based week key or DST day count shifts a day and disagrees with the database's date_trunc('week') bucket.
A today, week, month or last-month results window opens at the wrong Property-local midnight or week start (US Sunday versus Monday), or last month crosses a year boundary wrongly.
A 'last N days' results window or its prior window shifts a day across DST or the Property's timezone, or the two windows overlap or differ in length.
A Response Target deadline or reminder is computed from the wrong start or duration, or a reply at or after the due instant is classed on time.
A retention cutoff reaches rows before their full horizon, for example a month-end date rolling forward instead of clamping when subtracting months.
Google review content outlives its 30-day clock, the clock is reset by something other than a successful fetch, or the refresh-due lead time is wrong.
